result.title: Skill-Composer: Requirement-Driven Skill Selection from Multiple Marketplaces
result.summary: Agent skills have become the primary vehicle through which agents reuse specialized capabilities, yet public skill marketplaces provide skills with individual items: a query, whether matched through keyword or embedding similarity, returns a list of single skills ordered by relevance or by popularity. Such an interface cannot answer the question a developer actually faces: which set of skills should be installed to cover a task's complete requirement? The highest-ranked skills are often functionally redundant, while capabilities that are genuinely required remain uncovered. In this paper, we argue that skill acquisition should be reframed from ranking to set selection. We propose Skill-Composer, an agent-native framework that selects a non-redundant skill bundle for the user requirement, which aims to cover all available required capabilities and report any gaps. Specifically, it clarifies user requirements into atomic requirement points, retrieves and merges candidate skills across fragmented marketplaces, decomposes each candidate's capabilities, and progressively discards overlapping ones, so that each retained skill provides different capabilities. This moves the decision of which skills to acquire from the developer to the agent itself. We position this reframing and sketch its workflow.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张把 agent 技能获取从「按相关性排序单个技能」重构为「集合选择」，提出 Skill-Composer：将用户需求分解为原子需求点、跨多个技能市场检索并合并候选、分解候选能力并逐步剔除重叠项，以组成覆盖全部所需能力且非冗余的技能包并报告缺口；目前仅给出定位与流程草图。
AI.relevance_reason: 「原子需求—能力覆盖—冗余剔除—缺口报告」这一目标结构可能为视觉证据或工具子集选择、以及覆盖不足时是否继续 LOOK 的停止判据提供类比线索；但该工作面向 agent 技能市场而非多模态推理，联系需较多核查。
